YC-backed Neuron Industries Launches to Build a New Industrial Controller as the Engineers Who Program the Old Ones Retire
The AI-native industrial controller lets engineers without controls training retrofit legacy machines and program new automation in plain English, as the workforce that maintains today's PLCs retires

Neuron Industries is introducing an industrial controller built for the AI era, using plain English to generate production control logic while helping manufacturers reduce controls projects from weeks to hours.

, a Y Combinator-backed industrial hardware technology company, today announced their public launch. Neuron Industries builds the controller that runs automated machinery, along with the software stack that covers its real-time runtime to cloud connectivity.

The goal is straightforward: to let engineers, without any prior control engineering training, write, verify, and change the logic themselves for the machines and factories they build. The company's first product, an industrial controller called the Cortex AIC, is in paid customer pilots.

The timing is poor. Reindustrialization and the data center buildout are both pushing demand for additional industrial capacity up while the pool of engineers qualified to commission and maintain it thins out. The usual response is to send existing staff out for training, which takes a considerable amount of time to convert into working competence.

"Neuron's mission is to drop the barrier to entry for industrial automation to the floor," said Dennis Ren, co-founder and CEO of Neuron Industries. "We want to enable not only faster and cheaper implementation of automation with existing factories, but also onboard a new wave of under-automated manufacturers to help re-industrialize America one machine at a time."

"Software engineering got 30 years of continuous innovation: version control, testing, code review, and fast feedback," said Kenneth Rhee, co-founder and CTO. "Controls engineering got almost none of it, and it is running the physical world. The goal is to enable engineers to develop industrial hardware at the speed of software."
Neuron Industries is based in El Segundo, California, and is part of Y Combinator's S26 batch. Organizations that build machines or factories can reach the company at hello@neuronindustries.com.

Neuron Industries Raises $10 Million Seed Round to Accelerate Industrial Automation

Neuron Industries, an industrial hardware and software company building an AI-native industrial controller, announced a $10 million seed round following its public launch in August. The oversubscribed round was co-led by FCVC and Obvious Ventures, with participation from Y Combinator, Thin Line Capital, Zee Prime Capital and Founder Factor.

Ren was the founding electrical engineer at Hawthorne-based Freeform where he built the control stack behind an autonomous metal 3D-printing factory. He found that off-the-shelf controllers failed to deliver the performance and flexibility demanded by the application.

Neuron’s Cortex AI Controller and Synapse development environment let engineers describe machine behavior and build user interfaces, generate readable control code and test it before deployment. It is focused on companies that are building new production plants, factories and machines, helping teams establish their controls platform from the earliest stages of design.
